rules.rule: Minimum bolt spacing (center-to-center)
rules.source_quote: The distance between centers of standard, oversized, or slotted holes shall not be less than 2⅔ times the nominal diameter, d, of the fastener

rules.rule: Minimum clear distance between bolt holes (or slots)
rules.source_quote: the clear distance between bolt holes or slots shall not be less than d

rules.rule: Maximum bolt spacing — painted members, or unpainted not subject to atmospheric corrosion
rules.units: t = thickness of thinner connected part
rules.source_quote: In painted members or unpainted members not subject to atmospheric corrosion, the spacing shall not exceed the lesser of 24 times the thickness of the thinner part or 12 in.

rules.rule: Maximum bolt spacing — unpainted weathering steel exposed to atmospheric corrosion
rules.units: t = thickness of thinner connected part
rules.source_quote: In unpainted members used in exposed conditions subject to atmospheric corrosion, the spacing shall not exceed the lesser of 14 times the thickness of the thinner part or 7 in.

rules.rule: Minimum edge distance — ½ in. bolt (standard hole, any edge direction)
rules.source_quote: The distance from the center of a standard hole to an edge of a connected part in any direction shall not be less than either the applicable value from Table J3.4 or Table J3.4M

rules.rule: Minimum edge distance — ⅝ in. bolt (standard hole)
rules.source_quote: Table J3.4 minimum edge distance for ⅝ in. bolt diameter

rules.rule: Minimum edge distance — ¾ in. bolt (standard hole)
rules.source_quote: Table J3.4 minimum edge distance for ¾ in. bolt diameter

rules.rule: Minimum edge distance — ⅞ in. bolt (standard hole)
rules.source_quote: Table J3.4 minimum edge distance for ⅞ in. bolt diameter

rules.rule: Minimum edge distance — 1 in. bolt (standard hole)
rules.source_quote: Table J3.4 minimum edge distance for 1 in. bolt diameter

rules.rule: Minimum edge distance — 1⅛ in. bolt (standard hole)
rules.source_quote: Table J3.4 minimum edge distance for 1⅛ in. bolt diameter

rules.rule: Minimum edge distance — 1¼ in. bolt (standard hole)
rules.source_quote: Table J3.4 minimum edge distance for 1¼ in. bolt diameter

rules.rule: Minimum edge distance — bolt diameter over 1¼ in. (standard hole)
rules.value: 1.25d (post-2010 single-column value; NOT the superseded 1.75d two-column value)
rules.source_quote: Table J3.4: for bolt diameters over 1¼ in., minimum edge distance = 1.25d

rules.rule: Maximum edge distance
rules.value: 12t, but not more than 6 in. (150 mm)
rules.source_quote: The distance from the center of a fastener to the edge of a connected part shall not exceed the lesser of 12 times the thickness of the connected part or 6 in.

rules.rule: Standard hole diameter — ½ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: AISC 360-22 Table J3.3: ½ in. bolt nominal diameter → 9/16 in. standard hole

rules.rule: Standard hole diameter — ⅝ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: AISC 360-22 Table J3.3: ⅝ in. bolt → 11/16 in. standard hole

rules.rule: Standard hole diameter — ¾ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: AISC 360-22 Table J3.3: ¾ in. bolt → 13/16 in. standard hole

rules.rule: Standard hole diameter — ⅞ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: AISC 360-22 Table J3.3: ⅞ in. bolt → 15/16 in. standard hole

rules.rule: Standard hole diameter — 1 in. bolt
rules.source_quote: AISC FAQ: Table J3.3 is based upon the RCSC Specification Table 3.1; for 1 in. bolt the standard hole is 1⅛ in. (d + 1/8 in. increment begins at 1 in. nominal)

rules.rule: Standard hole size formula by bolt diameter
rules.value: d + 1/16 in. for bolts up to ⅞ in.; d + 1/8 in. for bolts 1 in. and larger
rules.source_quote: RCSC Table 3.1 footnote: increment is 1/16 in. for bolt diameters through ⅞ in., 1/8 in. for 1 in. and larger

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 120 (e.g. A325), ½ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2 Minimum Bolt Pretension Tm: ½ in., Group 120 = 12 kips; Tm = 0.70 × specified minimum tensile strength × tensile stress area, rounded to nearest kip

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 120, ⅝ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: ⅝ in., Group 120 = 19 kips

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 120, ¾ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: ¾ in., Group 120 = 28 kips

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 120, ⅞ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: ⅞ in., Group 120 = 39 kips

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 120, 1 in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: 1 in., Group 120 = 51 kips

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 120, 1⅛ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: 1⅛ in., Group 120 = 64 kips

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 120, 1¼ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: 1¼ in., Group 120 = 81 kips

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 150 (e.g. A490), ½ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: ½ in., Group 150 = 15 kips

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 150, ¾ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: ¾ in., Group 150 = 35 kips

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 150, ⅞ in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: ⅞ in., Group 150 = 49 kips

rules.rule: Minimum pretension — Group 150, 1 in. bolt
rules.source_quote: Table 5.2: 1 in., Group 150 = 64 kips

rules.rule: Pretension derivation formula
rules.value: Tm = 0.70 × (specified minimum tensile strength × tensile stress area), rounded to nearest kip
rules.source_quote: The specified minimum pretensions … are based on 70 percent of the tensile strength … rounded to the nearest kip

rules.rule: Grip (basis for bolt-length selection)
rules.value: Total thickness of the connected plies the bolt passes through, EXCLUDING washers and direct-tension indicators (DTIs)
rules.source_quote: Grip. The total thickness of material a bolt passes through, exclusive of washers or direct-tension indicators.

rules.rule: Bolt length must achieve sufficient thread engagement
rules.value: Length chosen so the installed bolt end is at least flush with (or beyond) the outer face of the nut — develops the bolt's strength
rules.source_quote: The bolt length used shall be such that, when installed, sufficient thread engagement (as defined in the Glossary) is achieved. [Glossary:] … the available bolt threads extending beyond or at least flush with the outer face of the nut; a condition that develops the strength of the bolt.

rules.rule: Selecting bolt length from grip
rules.value: length = grip + add-to-grip value (RCSC Table C-2.2), rounded to nearest ¼ in. (½ in. for lengths over 6 in.)
rules.citation: RCSC 2020 Commentary §2.7, Table C-2.2 (more extensive: Carter 1996, AISC Engineering Journal 2Q)
rules.source_quote: To determine the required bolt length, the value shown in Table C-2.2 should be added to the grip … The length determined by the use of Table C-2.2 should be adjusted to the nearest ¼-in. increment (or ½-in. increment for lengths exceeding 6 in.). A more extensive table … is available (Carter, 1996).

rules.rule: Washer thickness added to grip when selecting bolt length
rules.value: +5/32 in. per ASTM F436 flat washer; +5/16 in. per beveled washer (added to grip before length selection)
rules.source_quote: For each ASTM F436 washer that is used, add 5/32 in.; for each beveled washer, add 5/16 in.

rules.rule: Minimum fillet weld leg — thinner part ≤ ¼ in. (6 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.4 Minimum Size of Fillet Welds: thickness of thinner part joined — to ¼ in. (6 mm) inclusive → minimum fillet weld size 1/8 in. (3 mm)

rules.rule: Minimum fillet weld leg — thinner part over ¼ in. to ½ in. (13 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.4: over ¼ in. to ½ in. (13 mm) → 3/16 in. (5 mm)

rules.rule: Minimum fillet weld leg — thinner part over ½ in. to ¾ in. (19 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.4: over ½ in. to ¾ in. (19 mm) → ¼ in. (6 mm)

rules.rule: Minimum fillet weld leg — thinner part over ¾ in. (19 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.4: over ¾ in. (19 mm) → 5/16 in. (8 mm)

rules.rule: Maximum fillet weld size — along edge of material less than ¼ in. thick
rules.source_quote: Along edges of material less than ¼ in. (6 mm) thick, the maximum size of the fillet weld shall equal the thickness of the material

rules.rule: Maximum fillet weld size — along edge of material ¼ in. or thicker
rules.value: t − 1/16 in. (2 mm), unless weld is detailed to be built out to full throat
rules.source_quote: Along edges of material ¼ in. (6 mm) or more in thickness, the maximum size of the fillet weld shall be 1/16 in. (2 mm) less than the thickness of the material

rules.rule: Effective throat of equal-leg fillet weld
rules.value: 0.707 × leg (w); the shortest distance from root to face of the diagrammatic weld
rules.source_quote: The effective throat of a fillet weld is the shortest distance from the root to the face of the diagrammatic weld

rules.rule: Minimum fillet weld length (for strength design)
rules.value: ≥ 4 × nominal leg size; else effective size = ¼ of its actual length
rules.source_quote: The minimum length of a fillet weld designed for strength purposes shall be at least four times the nominal size … if longer than four times the nominal size, the effective size shall be not more than one-quarter of its length

rules.rule: Minimum intermittent fillet weld segment length
rules.source_quote: Intermittent fillet welds shall have a minimum length of not less than four times the weld size, with a minimum of 1½ in. (38 mm)

rules.rule: End-loaded fillet weld length reduction (β factor)
rules.units: l = weld length, w = leg size
rules.source_quote: β = 1.2 − 0.002(l/w) ≤ 1.0 (Eq. J2-1); where l/w > 300, the effective length shall be taken as 180w

rules.rule: Minimum PJP groove weld effective throat — thinner part ≤ ¼ in. (6 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.3 Minimum Effective Throat Size of PJP Groove Welds: to ¼ in. (6 mm) inclusive → 1/8 in. (3 mm)

rules.rule: Minimum PJP groove weld effective throat — thinner part over ¼ in. to ½ in. (13 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.3: over ¼ in. to ½ in. (13 mm) → 3/16 in. (5 mm)

rules.rule: Minimum PJP groove weld effective throat — thinner part over ½ in. to ¾ in. (19 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.3: over ½ in. to ¾ in. (19 mm) → ¼ in. (6 mm)

rules.rule: Minimum PJP groove weld effective throat — thinner part over ¾ in. to 1½ in. (38 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.3: over ¾ in. to 1½ in. (38 mm) → 5/16 in. (8 mm)

rules.rule: Minimum PJP groove weld effective throat — thinner part over 1½ in. to 2¼ in. (57 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.3: over 1½ in. to 2¼ in. (57 mm) → 3/8 in. (10 mm)

rules.rule: Minimum PJP groove weld effective throat — thinner part over 2¼ in. to 6 in. (150 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.3: over 2¼ in. to 6 in. (150 mm) → ½ in. (13 mm)

rules.rule: Minimum PJP groove weld effective throat — thinner part over 6 in. (150 mm)
rules.source_quote: Table J2.3: over 6 in. (150 mm) → 5/8 in. (16 mm)

rules.rule: Nominal bearing strength at bolt hole — deformation is a design consideration (standard/oversized/short-slotted, or long-slotted parallel to force)
rules.units: kips (d = bolt dia. in., t = ply thickness in., Fu = connected material strength ksi)
rules.source_quote: Rn = 2.4dtFu (J3-6a)

rules.rule: Nominal bearing strength at bolt hole — deformation not a design consideration
rules.source_quote: Rn = 3.0dtFu (J3-6b)

rules.rule: Nominal tearout strength — deformation is a design consideration
rules.units: kips (lc = clear distance in force direction, in.)
rules.source_quote: Rn = 1.2 lc t Fu (J3-6c)

rules.rule: Nominal tearout strength — deformation not a design consideration
rules.source_quote: Rn = 1.5 lc t Fu (J3-6d)

rules.rule: LRFD resistance factor for bolt bearing and tearout
rules.source_quote: φ = 0.75 (LRFD) and Ω = 2.00 (ASD) for bolt bearing and tearout provisions

rules.rule: ASD safety factor for bolt bearing and tearout
rules.source_quote: φ = 0.75 (LRFD) and Ω = 2.00 (ASD) for bolt bearing and tearout provisions

rules.rule: Preferred grade for wide-flange W-shapes
rules.value: ASTM A992 — Fy = 50 ksi, Fu = 65 ksi; yield-to-tensile ratio capped at 0.85
rules.citation: AISC 360-22 Table A3.1 + AISC SteelWise June 2022
rules.source_quote: A992: Fy min 50 ksi, Fu min 65 ksi; Fy/Fu ≤ 0.85 (ductility cap)

rules.rule: Preferred grade for HP bearing piles and plates/bars
rules.value: ASTM A572 Grade 50 — Fy = 50 ksi, Fu = 65 ksi
rules.citation: AISC 360-22 Table A3.1 + AISC SteelWise June 2022
rules.source_quote: AISC SteelWise 2022 recommendation: HP piles and plates → A572-50

rules.rule: Preferred grade for C and MC channels (360-22 update)
rules.value: ASTM A992 — Fy = 50 ksi, Fu = 65 ksi (360-22 updated preference from A36)
rules.source_quote: 360-22 updated preference: channels (C/MC) now commonly A992, previously A36

rules.rule: Grade for angles (L shapes)
rules.value: A36 — Fy = 36 ksi, Fu = 58 ksi (transitioning to 50-ksi grades)
rules.source_quote: L shapes: A36 (Fy 36 ksi, Fu 58 ksi); transitioning to 50-ksi grades per SteelWise

rules.rule: Preferred grade for rectangular/square HSS (360-22 update)
rules.value: ASTM A500 Grade C — Fy = 50 ksi, Fu = 62 ksi (360-22 update from Grade B: rect was 46/58)
rules.source_quote: 360-22 preference: HSS rectangular → A500 Grade C (Fy 50 ksi, Fu 62 ksi); Grade B (Fy 46 ksi, Fu 58 ksi for rect) no longer preferred

rules.rule: Preferred grade for round HSS (360-22 update)
rules.value: ASTM A500 Grade C — Fy = 46 ksi, Fu = 62 ksi
rules.source_quote: 360-22 preference: HSS round → A500 Grade C (Fy 46 ksi, Fu 62 ksi)

rules.rule: Grade for premium HSS (tight tolerance)
rules.value: ASTM A1085 — Fy = 50 ksi, Fu = 65 ksi (supplier-corroborated Fu)
rules.source_quote: A1085 HSS: Fy 50 ksi; Fu = 65 ksi per AISC Basic Design Values; tighter tolerances than A500

rules.rule: Grade for standard pipe (round)
rules.value: ASTM A53 Grade B — Fy = 35 ksi, Fu = 60 ksi
rules.source_quote: A53 Grade B: Fy 35 ksi, Fu 60 ksi

rules.rule: Grade for anchor rods
rules.source_quote: F1554 anchor rods: Grade designation = Fy in ksi (Gr. 36, 55, 105)

rules.rule: Bolt grade — Group 120 (formerly ASTM A325)
rules.value: F3125 Group 120; minimum tensile strength Fu = 120 ksi
rules.source_quote: ASTM F3125 consolidates A325 (and A325M) into Group 120; minimum Fu = 120 ksi

rules.rule: Bolt grade — Group 150 (formerly ASTM A490)
rules.value: F3125 Group 150; minimum tensile strength Fu = 150 ksi
rules.source_quote: ASTM F3125 consolidates A490 (and A490M) into Group 150; minimum Fu = 150 ksi

rules.rule: Weld electrode grade (common structural steel)
rules.source_quote: E70XX classification: 70 = minimum tensile strength in ksi (FEXX); matched to A36/A572/A992 base metal per AWS D1.1 Table 3.1
